newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: SADC chief says group must help resolve Zaire war.
newsitem.headline: SADC chief says group must help resolve Zaire war.

text.p: Southern African Development Community chief Kaire Mbuende says the Africa trade groupings' 12 members must help resolve the civil war in neighbouring Zaire.

"Zaire is not a member of SADC but we have to keep our house in order...to make sure that the values that we develop in the SADC region are defended and protected," Mbuende said on Thursday during the signing of a cooperation agreement with Belgium in Gaborone, Botswana.
Zaire shares borders with SADC members Angola, Zambia and Tanzania. Other members are South Africa, Botswana, Zimbabwe, Namibia, Mozambique, Lesotho, Swaziland, Mauritius and Malawi.

"We want peace and democracy in Zaire. Our heads of state are actively engaged to ensure that ultimately peace and democracy come to Zaire for the sake of the people of that country and for the sake of the people of the region and Africa," Mbuende added.
Belgium's ambassador to Botswana Leo Willems said there could be no peace and stability in Zaire without democratic elections.
"Elections will be delayed, they might not take place this year, but they will take place...but without that there will be no solution in Zaire," he said.
